references.text: Luke tells us that Joseph's family returned to Nazareth, the town where Jesus grew up – this confirms that Nazareth was the place "where he was brought up".
Describes Jesus' upbringing in Nazareth, where he was subject to his parents and grew in wisdom – the background for why Nazareth was his hometown.
Matthew tells us that Joseph's family settled in Nazareth, and that Jesus was called a Nazarene, confirming Nazareth as Jesus' home.
Jesus comes to his hometown and teaches in the synagogue there, a parallel to Luke's account of Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth.
Mark's parallel account of Jesus coming to his hometown and teaching in the synagogue on the Sabbath.
Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and began to teach – a pattern showing his custom of attending synagogue worship.
Paul, according to his custom, went into the synagogue and spoke to them from the Scriptures for three Sabbaths – a parallel to Jesus' habit of going to the synagogue on the Sabbath.

Paul and Barnabas entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down, and after the reading of the Law and the Prophets they were invited to speak – a parallel to the custom of Scripture reading in the synagogue.
Refers to the established practice of reading from Moses in the synagogues every Sabbath, which sheds light on the custom Jesus participated in.
Ezra stood up and read from the Book of the Law before the people – an early example of the custom of public Scripture reading that Jesus followed in the synagogue.
Jesus went down to Capernaum and taught the people on the Sabbath days, confirming his habit of teaching in the synagogues on the Sabbath.
